title: In China, the AI bubble has burst
content:
Oct 26 (Reuters) - While global tech stocks teeter, in China they have already crashed as lofty valuations collapse under worries about AI demand and curbs on Chinese exports.
The meltdown, tanking the mainland STAR50 index of AI and semiconductor leaders by 40% in less than four months and vaporising some $480 billion in market value, is an ill omen for wobbly world markets and a dampener on China's efforts at encouraging its savers into stocks to fund the AI boom.
It has also slammed the brakes on a rally running two years, since economic stimulus promises sent shares soaring, and has stalled Beijing's push to break with a long boom-bust pattern and drive a "slow bull" market that delivers reliable performance. China's broad blue-chip index has dropped about 20% from highs made in June.
"The stock market later evolved into a speculative crazy bull," said Beijing-based fund manager Dong Baozhen. "And now we see the bubble bursting."
The reversal reflects a rally that ran to higher heights than markets in the West or elsewhere in Asia, and compares with a mere prick to US AI stocks, which have led a 6% drawdown in the Nasdaq from a record high scaled three weeks ago.
There has been no obvious selling trigger in China, although traders said high prices, tax bills and the threat of the US or other nations banning Chinese equipment in data centres all contributed.
With AI stocks running to 42% of China's market capitalisation and 57% of turnover across mainland-listed A-shares and Hong Kong's H-shares, according to Goldman Sachs, few in a market dominated by small investors have escaped pain.
RETAIL FAVOURITES SLIDE
Shares in robot-maker Unitree, 8,000 times oversubscribed by retail buyers at listing, have halved since they started trading in August, and chipmaker CXMT has lost more than a quarter of its value in the past month.
Chipmakers MetaX Integrated Circuits and Moore Threads Technology, which leapt 700% and 400% respectively on their market debuts last year, have also halved in value since July.
Chen Wensheng, a small business owner and investor from China's southern Hainan, said he bought into the rally emboldened by what he felt was official support for the likes of Unitree, which counted state-backed funds as investors. But Chen and his friends are now nursing losses.
Frustration that an investment theme backed by Beijing has ended so badly has driven many investors into defensive assets and is likely to slow equity fundraising by tech firms.
Shares in optical parts makers Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink Technology are down roughly 60% from highs in June and July, in part as Washington moves towards banning the one-time darlings from supplying US data centres.

report.summary: China’s AI stock bubble has burst, with the STAR50 index down 40% in under four months and roughly $480 billion in market value erased.
report.background: China’s AI and semiconductor stocks had rallied for two years after stimulus promises, with retail investors piling into names such as Unitree, CXMT, MetaX and Moore Threads. Beijing hoped to create a “slow bull” market that would draw savers into equities and help fund its AI ambitions. But valuations became stretched: Goldman Sachs says AI stocks reached 42% of China’s market capitalization and 57% of turnover across mainland A-shares and Hong Kong H-shares. Worries about AI demand, export curbs and possible bans on Chinese equipment in US data centers then triggered a sharp reversal, contrasting with a milder drawdown in US tech.
key_points: The selloff is severe and broad. The STAR50 index of AI and semiconductor leaders has fallen 40% in less than four months, wiping out about $480 billion in market value, while China’s blue-chip index is down roughly 20% from June highs. Traders cite high prices, tax bills and fears of US or other bans on Chinese data-center equipment, rather than one obvious trigger.

Retail investors are bearing the brunt. AI stocks account for 42% of China’s market capitalization and 57% of turnover, and the market is dominated by small investors. Robot-maker Unitree has halved since its August listing; CXMT is down more than a quarter in a month; MetaX and Moore Threads have halved since July after huge debut gains.

The crash undermines Beijing’s market strategy. The reversal stalls a two-year rally and Beijing’s push to break China’s boom-bust pattern with a “slow bull” market that draws savers into stocks to fund AI. Frustrated investors are shifting to defensive assets, which is likely to slow equity fundraising by tech firms.

The global read-across is cautionary. China’s meltdown is an ill omen for wobbly world markets, even though US AI stocks have seen only a modest pullback, with the Nasdaq down about 6% from a record. Export restrictions are already hitting Chinese optical suppliers: Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink are down roughly 60% from summer highs.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the burst bubble is a valuation reset more than a technology verdict. Chinese chip and AI firms will find equity fundraising harder and may face consolidation, while investors demand revenue and cash flow rather than speculative growth. Developers could see fewer generously funded startups and more disciplined hiring, but also cheaper talent and a focus on practical applications. Regular users may not feel an immediate change, though tighter funding and export controls could slow some product rollouts and raise supply-chain costs. Globally, the episode warns that AI enthusiasm can outrun demand and policy support, making markets more sensitive to export bans and earnings disappointments.
report.tools: To track this story, use OpenBB or yfinance for open-source market data and research, AKShare for Chinese A-share and Hong Kong data, and TradingView or Yahoo Finance for STAR50, Nasdaq and AI-stock charts. For policy and export-control context, follow Reuters, Goldman Sachs research and company filings. These are monitoring tools, not investment advice.
